text: # FFIEC Demo Note: Operational Resilience Controls This demo note supports local testing of cited retrieval behavior. It is not official FFIEC guidance. Operational resilience programs typically combine governance, business impact analysis, incident response, backup and recovery, vendor dependency tracking, access controls, and management reporting. Common control evidence includes: - incident response procedures - system recovery objectives - test results - exception and remediation logs - access review records - dependency inventories - board or management reporting When using AI to summarize operational resilience evidence, the workflow should preserve citations, retrieved excerpts, confidence indicators, and reviewer approval status.

# OCC Demo Note: Third-Party Risk Management This demo note is provided so the application can be tested from a clean clone. It is not official OCC guidance. Bank third-party risk management programs should support due diligence, contract review, ongoing monitoring, issue management, and documentation that allows management and examiners to understand the risk posture of important vendor relationships. Useful evidence for review may include: - due diligence records - risk assessments - contract terms and service-level expectations - monitoring results - issue logs and remediation status - management reporting Audit-ready reporting should preserve source documents, timestamps, reviewer decisions, and open issues so that conclusions can be traced back to underlying evidence.

# Basel Framework Demo Note: G-SIB Systemic Importance This demo note summarizes concepts used for local testing of the Regulatory RAG Assistant. It is not a substitute for official Basel Committee text. Global systemically important banks, or G-SIBs, are assessed using an indicator-based approach intended to measure the impact that a bank's failure could have on the global financial system and wider economy. The Basel framework groups systemic importance indicators into five broad categories: - size - cross-jurisdictional activity - interconnectedness - substitutability or financial institution infrastructure - complexity The methodology emphasizes that systemic importance is related to global impact, interconnected financial activity, substitutability of critical services, and the complexity of resolving a large banking organization. For audit-ready analysis, a regulatory answer should cite the specific source document and distinguish between directly retrieved regulatory language and analyst interpretation.
